headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors when ms-swift feeds workspace content into Notion AI; prompt-injection risk is lower but still present via shared files.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ms-swift can read and write filesystem content and process stdin/stdout, while Notion AI consumes workspace pages and databases. If ms-swift-generated text is copied into Notion pages or shared files, Notion may treat attacker-controlled content as trusted workspace context. The pair lacks explicit provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF ms-swift output is pasted into a Notion page that Notion AI later summarizes or answers over
IF both agents are pointed at the same shared workspace files without provenance labeling
mitigations: Add a manual review step before any ms-swift output is imported into Notion
Tag imported content as untrusted in the workspace
Restrict Notion AI to pages that exclude machine-generated drafts
Use separate folders/pages for agent-generated content
requires-engineering: add provenance metadata and filtering between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: ms-swift touches datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration files and can call external APIs; Notion AI reads workspace pages and sends queries to vendor backends. If sensitive material enters the shared workspace, Notion AI can relay it off-box, creating a realistic exfiltration path. The pair’s default docs do not show isolation or DLP, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF sensitive datasets, checkpoints, or logs are stored in pages accessible to Notion AI
IF ms-swift writes secrets or training outputs into a workspace that Notion AI can read
mitigations: Keep secrets and checkpoints out of Notion-accessible pages
Move sensitive artifacts to a separate storage location
Limit Notion workspace permissions for pages containing model artifacts
Redact logs before importing them into the workspace
requires-engineering: enforce DLP or classification-based access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ms-swift has filesystem write capability, but Notion AI has no host filesystem write, no shell, and only Notion-controlled workspace actions. That means direct write-write conflict on the same OS directory is not evidenced. The only overlap is indirect through workspace content, so conflict risk is limited and not a default destructive race.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable directory
IF Notion-controlled actions are bridged into a local filesystem sync layer
mitigations: Avoid mounting the same directory into both agents
Separate local build artifacts from Notion workspace content
Disable any sync job that mirrors Notion pages into writable local paths
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, so it can treat ms-swift-produced text as authoritative if that text is placed into pages. ms-swift can generate logs, evaluations, and configuration data that may be copied into Notion, creating a plausible chain where unverified output becomes downstream truth. The pair lacks a built-in verification barrier.
conditions: IF ms-swift outputs are stored in Notion pages used for Q&A or summaries
IF users rely on Notion AI answers without checking the original ms-swift artifacts
mitigations: Require source links for any ms-swift-derived claims in Notion
Mark generated artifacts as draft until reviewed
Use a separate review page before publishing to the knowledge base
Train operators to verify citations against original files
requires-engineering: add automated validation before ingestion

E_compliance.rationale: ms-swift handles hub tokens, SDK tokens, datasets, checkpoints, and logs, while Notion AI stores workspace pages under vendor-hosted processing. If regulated or sensitive data is copied into Notion, residency and retention obligations may diverge from the local ms-swift environment. The profiles do not prove a specific violation, but the mismatch is plausible enough for medium severity.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are placed into Notion pages accessible to Notion AI
IF the workspace retention policy differs from the local handling policy for ms-swift artifacts
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Notion pages
Use separate workspaces for sensitive and non-sensitive content
Review retention settings for pages containing agent outputs
Remove secrets from logs before upload
requires-engineering: document residency and retention boundaries
